content.search: You might have been looking for a way out. But you clicked this link. It means a part of you still wants to stay.
content.block1: Right now you are in severe pain. It feels endless, and it feels like the only way to stop it is to stop existing.
content.block2: You do not want to die. You want the pain to stop. Those are two different things.
content.block3: The pain you feel is real. Your feelings matter. What you are going through is hard, and it is not your fault.
content.block4: Under extreme stress, the brain narrows perception to a dead end. That does not mean there is no way out - it means it is too hard to see right now.
content.block5: Feelings are not permanent. Even unbearable pain shifts with time. You have made it through dark times before.
content.block6: You do not have to fix your whole life tonight. Just get through this hour. These next ten minutes.
content.block7: There are people ready to listen right now. Without judgment or lectures. Free and anonymous.
content.block8: Reaching out is not giving up. It is giving yourself another chance. One conversation commits you to nothing, but can change everything.
content.block9: Please. Give yourself a little more time. Stay.
content.block10: This world needs you. Even if it does not feel like it right now.

meta.title: How to help someone in crisis | You are needed. Stay.
meta.description: Guide on how to recognize crisis signs and support someone thinking about suicide.

hero.title: How to help someone in crisis
hero.subtitle: If you are worried about someone on the edge - here is what you can do right now.

signs.title: Warning signs
signs.intro: People rarely state suicidal thoughts directly. Watch for these signals:
signs.s1: Direct or indirect statements: 'I can't do this anymore', 'Everyone would be better off without me'
signs.s2: Giving away belongings, saying goodbye, sudden tidying up
signs.s3: Sudden calm after long depression - could indicate a decision was made
signs.s4: Withdrawing from friends, family, and daily activities
signs.s5: Fixation on death and searching for methods online
signs.s6: Reckless behavior: substance abuse, dangerous driving
signs.s7: Severe mood swings from despair to unusual euphoria
signs.s8: Loss of interest in things that used to bring joy
signs.s9: Complaints of unbearable mental or physical pain
signs.note: If you notice 2-3 signs - do not wait. Take action.

steps.title: 5 steps of first aid
steps.s1text: Ask: 'Are you thinking about suicide?' Research proves direct questions do not increase risk - they show you are willing to talk about the hardest things.
steps.s2text: Do not interrupt or argue. Just listen. Your presence matters more than having perfect answers.
steps.s3text: Remove lethal means (medications, sharp objects). Do not leave the person alone if risk is high.
steps.s4text: Offer to call a helpline together or help schedule an appointment with a crisis specialist.
steps.s5text: Check in the next day and the next week. Consistent check-ins significantly reduce recurrent crises.

talk.title: What to say and what to avoid
talk.do1: 'I am here with you no matter what.'
talk.do2: 'Your pain is real and I see how heavy this is.'
talk.do3: 'You are not a burden to me. You matter.'
talk.do4: 'We will get through this together. Step by step.'
talk.do5: 'Thank you for trusting me. Let's figure out how to help you right now.'
talk.dont1: 'Others have it worse' / 'Cheer up, it will pass'

myth.title: The biggest myth
myth.text: 'Talking about suicide plants the idea.' This is false. Direct and compassionate questions reduce anxiety, validate pain, and lower risk.

yourself.title: Care for yourself
yourself.text1: Supporting someone in crisis takes a serious emotional toll. You cannot carry 100% responsibility alone.
yourself.text2: If it feels too heavy, reach out for support yourself. Helplines also support caregivers and loved ones.
yourself.text3: In an emergency with immediate danger, call emergency services: 112 or 911.

meta.title: It feels like... | You are needed. Stay.
meta.description: Six cognitive distortions that feel true during severe crisis, and why they mislead you.

hero.title: It feels like...
hero.subtitle: Severe pain distorts reality. Here are six thoughts that commonly emerge and why they are misleading.

seemsLike.intro: In crisis, the brain enters tunnel vision: it focuses only on worst interpretations. Just because a thought feels absolutely true does not make it a fact.

d1.validation: You feel like a burden because you are struggling and worry people are tired of your problems.
d1.reframe: People who care about you would rather listen to your pain thousands of times than attend your funeral once.
d1.try: Ask yourself: 'If my best friend was going through this, would I consider them a burden?'

d2.validation: Isolation makes you feel invisible when people haven't reached out recently.
d2.reframe: Most people are absorbed in their own stress and routine. Silence rarely means a lack of care.
d2.try: Text one person: 'Hey, I am having a rough time right now, can we stay in touch?'

d3.validation: Prolonged pain erases memory of feeling okay, making suffering feel permanent.
d3.reframe: 'Never' is a distortion. Emotional states are temporary. Conditions causing pain can be treated.
d3.try: Recall even one single moment in the past when things felt slightly lighter.

d4.thought: 4. 'I ruined everything, nothing can be fixed'
d4.validation: Mistakes and losses can feel like an absolute point of no return.
d4.reframe: As long as you are alive, almost everything can be adapted to or repaired. Death is the only truly irreversible outcome.
d4.try: Postpone any final decision by 24 hours. Commit only to getting through tonight.

d5.validation: Pressure to appear strong makes asking for help feel like failure.
d5.reframe: Reaching out when drowning is basic survival, not weakness.
d5.try: Call a crisis line right now. It is anonymous, free, and staffed by trained listeners.

d6.thought: 6. 'The world would be better without me'
d6.validation: A deeply dangerous distortion created by acute depressive states.
d6.reframe: Suicide does not end pain; it passes it on multiplied. Your presence matters.
d6.try: Stay here a bit longer. Breathe. Take a sip of water. One step at a time.

close.text: Thoughts are not facts. What your brain tells you right now is clouded by pain.
